implementation_notes: Scala traits compose by linearisation, so SOLID's inheritance rules map onto trait mixins rather than class chains. Prefer constructor injection with `val` parameters; use path-dependent types or `type X = ...` aliases for abstractions that are genuinely scoped; case classes give immutable value semantics for the abstraction side.
idiom_name: traits with linearisation + constructor injection + case classes
pitfalls: Trait linearisation makes conflicting members fail at compile time in confusing order — keep trait responsibilities disjoint.
Implicit parameters used as service location defeat DIP and hide the dependency graph.
Case classes with many parameters encourage passing unrelated things together (the primitive obsession / data clump trap).
